For each usable run give the image and approximate location, then note positions as integers in diatonic staff steps relative to the first note (0), preserving adjacent repeats. Prefer 6-14 or more consecutive notes where legible; describe uncertainty and stop at a gap or hidden span. Say which marks might be custos rather than sung notes. Report visible clef shape and line if secure; do not guess absolute pitch. Give a short literal reading of any accompanying words, with uncertainty, without completing from memory. If possible record two separate passages for later comparison. If no reliable continuous run of at least four notes remains after repeated pitches collapse, explain the visible limitation. A difficult image is not automatically unreadable: inspect the actual crops. Do not write readings of an image you could not view. Finish with coverage and limitations. Save the entire response as response.txt in this packet directory. Do not modify prompt, images, or packet.json.

text:
Image-only reading of packet 10

Orientation and surviving material
All six images were viewed. The written faces are upright as supplied: musical reading is left to right, with words below the staves. Images 001 and 002 show a largely blank binding/endleaf and two small tabs at its right edge, folded in and opened respectively. Images 003–006 are details of these tabs, not six independent musical passages. The large blank leaf is host material; readings below concern the reused tabs. The writing on the upper opened tab is not demonstrably musical underlay.

Image 003 (upper folded tab) has two horizontal red rules but no securely recognizable notes or words. Image 005 (upper opened tab) has two red rules, writing beneath them, and a lower flourish/signature-like inscription. There is no usable musical run on this face.

Images 004 and 006 each preserve two very short portions of five-line red staves, with dark angular/diamond-shaped noteheads. Image 004 shows right-hand ends of staves, with a vertical red border near the right. Image 006 shows left-hand starts, with vertical red rules and clef-like marks at the left. Neither view exposes enough music to bridge to the other face, so I do not join their sequences.

Clefs
Image 004 has no visible clef. In image 006, both staves have two large dark signs at the left: an open C-like shape around the second red line from the top (fourth from the bottom), and a taller F-like shape around the fourth line from the top (second from the bottom). The upper staff's lower sign also has a small mark to its right. These resemble paired clef indications; their exact graphic interpretation is less secure than the note positions. No absolute pitch is assigned. In particular, none of these large left-margin signs is included as a sung note.

Passage A: image 004, lower staff
Location: approximately x=140–360, y=800–930 in the displayed 606-by-1282 image. There are five complete consecutive noteheads. Their positions in diatonic staff steps relative to the first complete head are:

0, +1, +2, +1, 0

Adjacent motion: up one, up one, down one, down one.

The first complete diamond is on the second line from the bottom; the next is in the space above it; the tall-stemmed central head is on the middle line; the next is in the space below the middle line; the last is back on the second line from the bottom. The long stroke beneath the central head is a stem, not extra notes. No adjacent repeats are visible among these five.

There is also a cropped black head at the extreme left, around x=75, apparently one staff step above the first complete head. If accepted as a note, the six-head reading relative to that cropped head would be 0, -1, 0, +1, 0, -1. Its truncation makes the five-complete-head version preferable. The isolated small dark spot on a higher staff line is not counted as a note. The rightmost complete head here has no clear reason to be treated as a custos; it is part of the continuous descending group.

Text: the faded word between the staves seems to end in “are”, perhaps “…iare”; the preceding letters are not secure. I cannot confidently associate a full word with the lower sequence.

Passage B: image 006, lower staff
Location: approximately x=245–485, y=795–980 in the displayed 619-by-1325 image, after the large left clef-like signs. Five complete consecutive heads yield:

0, +2, 0, -1, 0

Adjacent motion: up two staff steps, down two, down one, up one.

The first head is on the middle red line. The second, with a long downward stem, is on the next red line above. The third returns to the middle line; the fourth is in the space immediately below it; the fifth, also with a downward stem, returns to the middle line. The red rules rise slightly to the right; these readings follow the local rules rather than comparing raw vertical image coordinates. No adjacent repeats occur. The five heads are reasonably secure; the fragment ends before any following group can be read.

Text: only incomplete letter shapes survive below this staff, including a dark group at the left and a tall isolated shape at the right. No full word is secure.

Additional short material
Image 004, upper staff, around x=145–245 and y=360–445: two complete heads rise by one staff step, 0, +1. A separate small, faint, diagonal mark farther right at x≈370 lies at roughly the second head's level. Its isolation at the staff end and different appearance make a custos plausible; it is not included in the sung sequence. This upper fragment alone is too short for the requested four-note minimum.

Image 006, upper staff, around x=275–540 and y=420–510: a connected dark figure is followed by an isolated diamond near the right cut edge. The connected figure's head/connecting-stroke boundaries are not secure enough for a reliable consecutive pitch sequence. The left part is near the middle line, and a low part at its right lies below that line, while the isolated diamond is approximately on the middle line. I do not decide whether the connecting figure contains two or more sung heads. The isolated right diamond could be an ordinary note in a passage cut off by the fragment; its being at the current fragment edge alone does not establish that it is a custos.

The word beneath this upper staff visibly ends “unt”; the initial shape could be r or s, giving “[r/s]unt”, but it is not secure. Additional writing is cut off at the right. I do not complete it.

Image 005 writing
The upper line has a large initial and a sequence approximately “…artinus”, with the beginning uncertain. The next line appears to end “…üller.” or “…uller.”; the beginning is clipped by the fold. These could be names/annotations rather than chant text. The low flourish and trailing characters cannot be transcribed reliably. No musical identification is inferred from this writing.

Coverage and limitations
Viewed images 001, 002, 003, 004, 005, and 006. The overviews confirm the location and folded/opened relationships; detailed readings use 004 and 006. Two separate five-note runs remain five notes after adjacent-repeat collapse, so short usable contours do survive. Neither provides six secure complete notes, let alone a long passage; the optional sixth note of Passage A is cropped. Cropping, folds, faded text, and the ambiguous connected upper-staff figure prevent a longer continuous reading. No hidden span, missing word, absolute pitch, or identity has been supplied.
